name: Wisconsin

sales.rateNote: 5% state sales and use tax on tangible personal property, certain digital goods and taxable services. Seventy counties add 0.5% (Milwaukee County 0.9%), and the city of Milwaukee adds 2%.

local.levies: counties (county tax), the city of Milwaukee (the only city sales tax), premier resort area municipalities, and local exposition districts (Milwaukee County lodging, food and beverage, rental car taxes)
local.capNote: County tax 0.5% (0.9% in Milwaukee County since January 1, 2024); city of Milwaukee 2% since January 1, 2024; premier resort area tax 0.5% to 1.25% in designated municipalities.

groceries.note: All food and food ingredients are exempt except candy, dietary supplements, prepared food and soft drinks.

otherRates.item: premier resort area tax (Wisconsin Dells, Lake Delton)
otherRates.note: Local tax on certain sellers in designated resort municipalities; 0.5% in Ephraim, Sister Bay, Rhinelander, Stockholm, Eagle River, Bayfield, and since July 1, 2026 Sturgeon Bay and Minocqua.

otherRates.item: Milwaukee County exposition taxes: food and beverage
otherRates.note: Local exposition district tax on food and beverages sold in Milwaukee County municipalities; also a 3% basic room tax, 7% additional room tax (city of Milwaukee) and 3% rental car tax.

sales.holidayNote: Wisconsin has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: 5% state use tax on items used, stored or consumed in Wisconsin on which no Wisconsin sales or use tax was paid, plus county/city use tax where applicable.

facts.text: The city of Milwaukee is the only Wisconsin municipality with its own sales tax: 2% since January 1, 2024, when Milwaukee County's rate also rose from 0.5% to 0.9%. Total in Milwaukee: 7.9%.
Sturgeon Bay and Minocqua adopted a 0.5% premier resort area tax effective July 1, 2026.
Seventy Wisconsin counties levy the 0.5% county sales tax.
Hotels in the city of Milwaukee charge an extra 7% room tax on top of the 3% basic room tax and sales taxes.
Candy and soft drinks are taxable even at grocery stores.

property.levied: local (counties, cities, villages and towns, school districts, technical colleges and special districts); bills are prepared by the municipality

assessment.text: Local assessors value property at market value as of January 1. Each municipality must be within 10% of market value at least once every five years (full value law); the DOR equalizes values to apportion county and school levies.

homestead.name: No homestead exemption (credits instead)
homestead.text: Wisconsin does not exempt part of a home's value. Tax bills show state-funded credits (school levy tax credit, first dollar credit, and the lottery and gaming credit for a primary residence), and low- and moderate-income residents can claim the income-based Homestead tax credit.

otherRelief.name: Homestead tax credit
otherRelief.text: Income-based credit paid directly to low- and moderate-income homeowners and renters; the amount depends on household income and property tax (renters count part of their rent).

otherRelief.name: Veterans and surviving spouses property tax credit
otherRelief.text: Refundable credit administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs; Wisconsin offers no property tax exemption for veterans.

otherRelief.name: Property tax deferral loan program
otherRelief.text: WHEDA loans to qualifying elderly homeowners, repaid when the home is sold or vacated.

dueDates.text: Unless the municipality sets another schedule: pay in full by January 31, or in installments with the first due January 31 and the second due July 31. A missed first installment makes the whole balance delinquent as of February 1.

facts.text: Tax bills are mailed by the third Monday in December and show the lottery and gaming credit and first dollar credit as deductions.
If a municipality stays outside the 10% full-value range for six consecutive years, the DOR orders a state-supervised revaluation.
Manufacturing property is assessed by the DOR, not by local assessors.
Some municipalities allow more than two installments; the local clerk confirms the schedule.

uncertain: Publication 201 (general sales tax guide) on the DOR site is an older edition still listing the 0.1% baseball stadium tax; current rates were taken from the DOR Tax Rates FAQ, which no longer lists a stadium tax.
Amounts of the lottery and gaming credit and school levy tax credit are not given in the 2026 Guide for Property Owners (omitted).
Whether local (county/city) sales taxes also exempt food is assumed from the base rule (local taxes apply to sales subject to state tax); not read explicitly.
The Wisconsin Legislature statute site (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov) did not respond; statutes were not read directly.
